What type of angle is $∠QPR,$ shown in the figure above?" :question/worked-solution "Notice that the vertex of $∠QPR$ is point $P,$ not point $R.$ So $∠QPR$ is *not* a straight angle.

We can think of $∠QPR$ as:

- a *null* angle, if we assume that it doesn't turn at all (diagram on the left), or

- A **right angle** has a measure of $90^\circ$. It corresponds to one-quarter of a full turn.![](images/15/155a1d6d2abd868b05674dec47ef4b20a5147d30cd328a5ba53d00dea271d65c.png)
- A **straight angle**, which is just a straight line, has a measure of $180^\circ$. It corresponds to one-half of a full turn.![](images/24/2423950f80de8354aee74c4f1daa6e42cf376caa0365307c76ebc7e09f96c8cf.png)

- A **null angle** has a measure of $0^\circ$. You can imagine "closing" the angle until the two sides of the angle overlap. In this case, we don't have any turn, so its measure is zero!![](images/f8/f86b7c1b7ba758fb6b07b6aeabd03395d29103b45e4cd220444b675f70a6e630.png)
- A **full angle** has a measure of $360^\circ$. You can imagine "opening" the angle until one of the sides goes all the way around. So, this is the angle between a ray and itself after it has made one full turn.![](images/cb/cbc9e288f4d3905357539a221954328ef0ac799531fab62f034364d32a7c0f29.png)

On a diagram, null and full angles can look the same, so it is up to us what we choose to call it." :tutorial/id #uuid "74e7b6f4-d873-55dc-81f9-6bf4148828b1" :tutorial/math-academy-id 2178
